body: Forward test of the management-tone-vs-delivery method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.55 (naive base rate 0.40) that: ICICI Lombard Q3 FY27 combined ratio is ≤103.5%. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Oct-2026): combined ratio 104.5% (102.7% ex-CAT losses of ₹118 cr) vs 103.9% in Q2 FY26; H1 FY27 105.2% (104.2% ex-CAT) vs 103.0% — H1 included provisions on motor third-party reserves after a Supreme Court judgement; management: 'we do not anticipate any need for any further requirement of provision' on that; industry motor combined ratio deteriorating (industry CoR 116.8% in Q1 FY27); GDPI +5.4% H1 vs industry +8.9%, fire de-growth easing. Q3 FY26 transcript (19-Jan-2026): Q3 FY26 combined ratio 103.1% (n basis); 9M FY26 103.1%. Q2 FY27 PAT ₹1,031 cr (+27.5%). Reasoning: Management sounds confident the TP reserve hit was one-off and Q3 is usually light on catastrophe losses; Q2 ex-CAT was already 102.7%. The delivery record on 'no further provisions' statements in Indian GI is mixed, but here the arithmetic supports it. We go above the backward-looking base. Resolution: YES if ICICI Lombard's reported combined ratio (n basis, including CAT losses, as stated in the Q3 FY27 press release/presentation) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≤103.5%. Source: ICICI Lombard Q3 FY27 press release / investor presentation (NSE). Resolve by 2027-02-15; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Naive: average of the last three reported quarterly combined ratios (Q3 FY26 103.1%, Q1 FY27 ~105.9% implied from H1, Q2 FY27 104.5%) is ~104.5%; chance of printing ≤103.5% is ~40%.
data.resolution_rule: YES if ICICI Lombard's reported combined ratio (n basis, including CAT losses, as stated in the Q3 FY27 press release/presentation) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≤103.5%.

title: Paper call: ICICI Lombard Q3 FY27 combined ratio is ≤103.5%
